original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Opt-in exact packed-integer backend for the complete dyadic transpose endpoint checkpoint, with a bound-planning pass and five alternating fresh-process benchmark pairs on the selected PR5599 word.
scope_change_reason: Restrict the replay-runtime card to the complete transpose endpoint checkpoint. This excludes native-state and whole-supplier acceleration and preserves a bounded same-fixture comparison.
bottleneck_link: Speeds a complete scalar endpoint checkpoint without removing any coefficient; native, caller, invoice and compiler checks stay external.
stop_rule: Ship the first verified backend speedup; no further tuning, new supplier audit or construction search.
evidence: PROOF.md; 4841 chronological dense-oracle words and wrong-endpoint controls; all 571536 selected checkpoint coefficients; source-bound five-pair BENCHMARK.json.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Can this opt-in endpoint backend be wired into a complete successor replay without changing its surrounding checks?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Only complete integration can establish a whole-replay gain.
open_questions.first_step: Bind one literal source call site, retain its original controls and compare the complete scientific output.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package benchmarks the transpose checkpoint only; no full supplier replay is performed.

overlap.entry_coverage: Cached search fetched 393 open PRs and 5635 Discussion records with complete pagination; local notes searched 62 of 8136 and were incomplete. Separate main README and distinctive merged searches were read.
overlap.related_predecessor: PR5757 accelerates native quadratic states and preserves the original reverse-column checkpoint. It does not supply this packed backend.
overlap.limitations: No arbitrary diff or unpublished-work coverage; no novelty certificate.
overlap.packed_predecessor: Sagar Thakrar PR1781 already uses exact packed integer matrices and signed-radix injectivity for Clifford recipes. This contribution claims only a new dyadic trace-bound planner/backend and measured scalar-transpose application, not that method.
